scenarios.title: Wrong DNS server
scenarios.desc: Websites stop opening, but Wi-Fi still shows connected.
scenarios.question: Ayaw mag-load ng mga website pero connected naman yung wifi ko

events.question: Ayaw mag-load ng mga website pero connected naman yung wifi ko

events.name: compare_with_normal
events.title: Comparing with the last time it worked
events.thought: First, compare with how this PC looked the last time the internet worked.

events.name: compare_with_normal
events.title: Comparing with the last time it worked
events.summary: Changed since the internet last worked: DNS servers on 'Wi-Fi' were 192.168.1.1, now 192.0.2.53, 2001:db8::53 (set manually).

events.name: check_dns
events.title: Checking DNS
events.summary: DNS servers on 'Wi-Fi': 192.0.2.53, 2001:db8::53 (set manually). None of them answer. A public DNS server (1.1.1.1) answers when asked directly. Windows CANNOT turn website names into addresses.

events.title: DNS is set to a server that does not answer
events.explanation: Someone or something set the DNS server by hand to an address that does not respond. The internet line works, but the PC cannot turn website names into addresses, so pages do not open.
evidence: Changed since the internet last worked: DNS servers on 'Wi-Fi' were 192.168.1.1, now 192.0.2.53, 2001:db8::53 (set manually).
DNS servers on 'Wi-Fi': 192.0.2.53, 2001:db8::53 (set manually). None of them answer. A public DNS server (1.1.1.1) answers when asked directly. Windows CANNOT turn website names into addresses.

fix.title: Set DNS back to automatic
fix.detail: Removes the hand-set DNS servers on 'Wi-Fi' so Windows uses the ones from your router again, then clears the DNS cache.

events.message: Fixed. I ran the checks again and the problem is gone.

checks.name: check_dns
checks.summary: DNS servers on 'Wi-Fi': 192.168.1.1 (automatic from the router). They answer. A public DNS server (1.1.1.1) answers when asked directly. Windows can turn website names into addresses.

events.message: Remembered: this is what this PC looks like when the internet works.
